questions.question_english: Which specific statutory provision of the POCSO Act, 2012 explicitly mandates that the Special Court must ensure that the child victim is not called repeatedly to testify in court?
options_english: Section 19 of the Act
Section 24 of the Act
Section 33(5) of the Act
Section 42 of the Act
questions.explanation_english:
Section 33 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 outlines the special procedure and powers of the Special Court.
Specifically, Section 33(5) states: 'The Special Court shall ensure that the child is not called repeatedly to testify in the court.'
This statutory safeguard is designed to prevent secondary victimization, reduce witness fatigue and anxiety, and ensure that trial procedures remain child-friendly. Other provisions mentioned:
- Section 19 deals with the mandatory reporting of offences.
- Section 24 covers the recording of a child's statement by police.
- Section 42 deals with alternative punishments under other laws.
Therefore, Section 33(5) is the exact provision protecting the child from repeated summons and appearances.
questions.explanation_hindi:
पॉक्सो अधिनियम, 2012 की धारा 33 विशेष न्यायालय की प्रक्रिया और शक्तियों का वर्णन करती है।
विशेष रूप से, धारा 33(5) स्पष्ट प्रावधान करती है: 'विशेष न्यायालय यह सुनिश्चित करेगा कि बालक को न्यायालय में गवाही (साक्ष्य) देने के लिए बार-बार न बुलाया जाए।' (The Special Court shall ensure that the child is not called repeatedly to testify in the court.)
इस प्रावधान का मूल उद्देश्य बालक को द्वितीयक उत्पीड़न (secondary victimization) और गंभीर मानसिक तनाव से बचाना है ताकि न्यायालय की प्रक्रिया बाल-सुलभ (child-friendly) बनी रहे।
अन्य विकल्प:
- धारा 19: अपराधों की अनिवार्य रिपोर्टिंग से संबंधित है।
- धारा 24: पुलिस द्वारा बालक के बयान दर्ज करने की प्रक्रिया से संबंधित है।
- धारा 42: अन्य कानूनों के तहत वैकल्पिक दंड से संबंधित है।
अतः सही प्रावधान धारा 33(5) है। इसलिए विकल्प C सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (c) Section 33(5)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Section 33(5) mandates that the Special Court shall ensure that the child victim is not called repeatedly to testify in court. Minimizing court appearances shields minor witnesses from repeated questioning, reduces emotional anxiety, and strictly upholds child-friendly procedural safeguards throughout all formal judicial trial proceedings.

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): An employee whose Form 26AS reflects less TDS than what was actually deducted as per their monthly salary pay slips can seamlessly claim the full tax credit while filing their Income Tax Return based solely on the pay slips.
Reason (R): Form 26AS is generated based on quarterly TDS returns filed by the employer; if the employer defaults in depositing the deducted tax or files the return with an incorrect PAN, the tax credit will not reflect in Form 26AS, resulting in an automated mismatch and demand notice from the CPC.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true. Under the automated e-filing and processing architecture of the Income Tax Department (CPC Bengaluru), tax credit claims in an Income Tax Return are strictly reconciled against the data pre-filled and validated in Form 26AS / Annual Information Statement (AIS). An employee cannot obtain tax credit merely on the strength of salary pay slips. questions.question_english:
Consider these statements regarding the Unni Krishnan judgment (1993):
I. It explicitly separated the right to elementary education from the right to higher education.
II. It declared that higher education is not a fundamental right.
III. It established the scheme for regulating admissions and fee structures in private professional colleges. 
Which of the above statements are correct?
options_english: I and II
II and III
I and III
I, II and III
questions.explanation_english: In Unni Krishnan (1993), the Supreme Court separated elementary education (a fundamental right up to age 14) from higher education (which is subject to economic capacity). key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) I, II and III

The Court created a detailed regulatory scheme for professional college admissions and fee structures to curb commercialization, making all three statements correct.

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The RPwD Act, 2016 mandates that the appropriate Government shall ensure that persons with disabilities enjoy the right to equality and a life with dignity.
Reason (R): The Act prohibits the deprivation of personal liberty of any person solely on the ground of disability.
In the context of the statements above, which of the following is correct?
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Both statements are correct statutory provisions under the RPwD Act, 2016, but Reason (R) is not the causal explanation of Assertion (A). Section 3(1) of the Act mandates that the appropriate Government shall ensure that persons with disabilities enjoy the right to equality, life with dignity, and respect for their integrity equally with others, directly giving effect to Articles 14 and 21 of the Constitution. Meanwhile, Section 4(1) provides that no person shall be deprived of his or her personal liberty only on the ground of disability. Although both are statutory rights safeguarding dignity and freedom, the prohibition against deprivation of personal liberty is an independent legal guarantee under Section 4 and does not logically or causally explain why the State must ensure equality and dignity under Section 3.
questions.explanation_hindi: दोनों कथन RPwD अधिनियम, 2016 के तहत सत्य वैधानिक प्रावधान हैं, परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है। धारा 3(1) यह अनिवार्य करती है कि समुचित सरकार यह सुनिश्चित करे कि दिव्यांग व्यक्ति समानता के अधिकार, गरिमापूर्ण जीवन तथा अपनी अखंडता के सम्मान का उपभोग दूसरों के समान करें (संविधान के अनुच्छेद 14 और 21 के अनुरूप)। वहीं, धारा 4(1) यह प्रावधान करती है कि किसी भी व्यक्ति को केवल दिव्यांगता के आधार पर उसकी व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता से वंचित नहीं किया जाएगा। दोनों प्रावधान महत्वपूर्ण मानवीय और मौलिक अधिकारों की रक्षा करते हैं, किंतु व्यक्तिगत स्वतंत्रता के हनन का निषेध, समानता व गरिमा सुनिश्चित करने के स्वतंत्र राज्यीय दायित्व का व्याख्यात्मक कारण नहीं है।
questions.topic: Constitutional Provisions for PwBD, EWS, SC, ST, and Disadvantaged Groups
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: correct explanation of A Section 3 mandates that the appropriate government ensures equality, life with dignity, and respect for integrity for persons with disabilities. The statute also prohibits the unlawful deprivation of personal liberty based solely on disability. While both statutory principles are true and established under the Act, prohibition of liberty deprivation serves as an independent guarantee rather than direct explanation.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following retirement terminal benefits and their tax exemptions applicable to government employees under the Income Tax Act:
I. Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity (DCRG) is fully exempt from income tax for government employees.
II. Leave encashment received at the time of retirement is fully exempt from income tax for government employees.
III. Commuted value of pension received upon retirement is fully exempt from income tax for government employees.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only

questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 10 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, statutory retirement benefits received by Central Government, State Government, and local authority employees enjoy comprehensive and unlimited tax exemptions:
1. Death-cum-Retirement Gratuity (DCRG): Fully exempt under Section 10(10)(i) without any monetary ceiling.
2. Leave Encashment: Under Section 10(10AA)(i), any payment received by government employees as leave encashment at the time of retirement/superannuation is entirely exempt from income tax without any monetary cap.
3. Commuted Pension: Under Section 10(10A)(i), any payment in commutation of pension received by government employees under the Civil Pensions (Commutation) Rules is 100% exempt from income tax.
Because all three statements (I, II, and III) are accurate, Option D is the correct choice.

questions.question_english: Universal Design for Learning (UDL) is an evidence-based framework designed to optimize teaching and learning for all diverse learners based on neurocognitive insights. Which of the following is NOT one of the three foundational principles of UDL?
options_english: Providing multiple means of Engagement (the 'why' of learning)
Providing multiple means of Representation (the 'what' of learning)
Providing multiple means of Action and Expression (the 'how' of learning)
Providing multiple means of Standardized Testing (the 'norm' of learning)
questions.explanation_english:
Universal Design for Learning (UDL), formulated by CAST (Center for Applied Special Technology) and deeply integrated into the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and RPwD Act guidelines, is anchored in cognitive neuroscience. It comprises three core principles:
1. Multiple means of Representation (The 'What' of learning): Presenting information, concepts, and perceptual content in varied modalities (visual, auditory, tactile, digital).
2. Multiple means of Action and Expression (The 'How' of learning): Offering flexible options for students to navigate learning environments and demonstrate mastery (writing, oral presentations, multimedia, physical models).
3. Multiple means of Engagement (The 'Why' of learning): Stimulating learners' interest, motivation, self-regulation, and persistence through diverse challenges and choices.
'Providing multiple means of Standardized Testing' is NOT a principle of UDL; in fact, UDL rejects rigid, one-size-fits-all standardized testing because it introduces construct-irrelevant barriers and fails to accurately assess diverse cognitive abilities.
questions.explanation_hindi:
सीखने के लिए सार्वभौमिक डिज़ाइन (UDL) संज्ञानात्मक तंत्रिका विज्ञान (Neuroscience) पर आधारित एक आधुनिक शैक्षणिक रूपरेखा है, जिसे राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति (NEP) 2020 में भी अत्यधिक महत्व दिया गया है। UDL तीन मूलभूत सिद्धांतों पर आधारित है:
1. अभ्यावेदन/प्रस्तुतीकरण के विविध साधन (Multiple means of Representation - 'अधिगम का क्या'): जानकारी और अवधारणाओं को विभिन्न प्रारूपों (दृश्य, श्रव्य, स्पर्शनीय, डिजिटल आदि) में प्रस्तुत करना।
2. क्रिया और अभिव्यक्ति के विविध साधन (Multiple means of Action and Expression - 'अधिगम का कैसे'): शिक्षार्थियों को अपने ज्ञान और कौशल को प्रदर्शित करने के लचीले विकल्प देना (लिखित, मौखिक, कलात्मक, प्रोजेक्ट आदि)।
3. जुड़ाव/संलग्नता के विविध साधन (Multiple means of Engagement - 'अधिगम का क्यों'): शिक्षार्थियों में प्रेरणा, रुचि और निरंतरता बनाए रखने के लिए विविध रणनीतियां अपनाना।
'मानकीकृत परीक्षण के विविध साधन' (Multiple means of Standardized Testing) UDL का सिद्धांत नहीं है; वास्तव में UDL कठोर और एक-समान मानकीकृत परीक्षण का विरोध करता है क्योंकि यह विविध शिक्षार्थियों की वास्तविक क्षमता का निष्पक्ष मूल्यांकन करने में असमर्थ होता है।

questions.question_english: If a school receives an application under the Right to Information (RTI) Act, 2005 seeking specific personal details regarding the exact amount of income tax (TDS) deducted and deposited for an individual teacher, how should the Principal (functioning as the Public Information Officer - PIO) legally respond?
options_english: Provide the detailed tax information immediately because the deduction involves public treasury remittances
Deny the request under Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act as it constitutes personal information having no relationship to any public activity or interest
Deny the information under Section 8(1)(a) of the RTI Act stating that tax matters impact the economic sovereignty of the nation

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 8(1)(j) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, personal information the disclosure of which has no relationship to any public activity or interest, or which would cause unwarranted invasion of the privacy of an individual, is exempt from disclosure unless the PIO or appellate authority is satisfied that the larger public interest justifies it. The Supreme Court of India in the landmark ruling of Girish Ramchandra Deshpande v. Central Information Commissioner (2012) categorically held that details of an employee's salary deductions, income tax returns, TDS statements, and personal assets qualify as personal information protected under Section 8(1)(j). Therefore, the Principal/PIO must deny disclosure unless a substantiated larger public interest is established by the applicant.

questions.explanation_english:
Section 2(m) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 defines 'inclusive education' as:
'a system of education wherein students with and without disability learn together and the system of teaching and learning is suitably adapted to meet the learning needs of different types of students with disabilities.'

This marks a profound pedagogical shift from 'Special Education' (which isolates students with disabilities into segregated institutions) and 'Integrated Education' (which places disabled children in general schools without adapting the underlying curriculum or infrastructure). Inclusive education demands systematic restructuring of physical classrooms, pedagogical materials, teacher training, and assistive aids to foster universal accessibility and belonging.

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 1(A)(c) of the Schedule to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, 'Cerebral Palsy' is classified under Locomotor Disability and is defined as a non-progressive condition characterized by abnormal motor control posture resulting from brain insult or injuries occurring in the pre-natal, peri-natal, or infant period of development. questions.question_english:
Read the following statements and select the correct option:
Assertion (A): A School Principal must immediately place a male teacher under suspension the moment a female teacher verbally complains about sexual harassment, without waiting for the ICC report.
Reason (R): Suspension is a mandatory interim relief under Section 12 of the POSH Act, 2013.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english:
Assertion (A) is completely FALSE: A Principal or employer cannot summarily suspend an employee solely on the basis of an informal verbal complaint without adhering to statutory due process. Under Section 9 of the POSH Act, a formal written complaint must be submitted to the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC), which then conducts an impartial inquiry in compliance with the principles of natural justice. Arbitrary suspension without a written complaint or committee recommendation violates administrative law.
Reason (R): In the context of the official answer key, Option D is designated as the correct choice, affirming that Assertion A is unequivocally false. Statutorily, under Section 12 of the POSH Act, interim relief measures (such as recommending transfer, granting up to 3 months paid leave, or other prescribed relief) are discretionary recommendations made by the ICC upon a written request from the aggrieved woman during an ongoing inquiry. Formal suspension pending inquiry is exercised by the Disciplinary Authority under applicable civil service rules (e.g., CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965). Because automatic suspension on verbal allegation is illegal, Assertion A is false, leading to Option D.
questions.explanation_hindi:
अभिकथन (A) पूरी तरह असत्य (गलत) है: कोई भी प्राचार्य अथवा नियोक्ता मात्र मौखिक शिकायत के आधार पर विधिक प्रक्रिया का पालन किए बिना किसी शिक्षक को सीधे निलंबित नहीं कर सकता। पॉश अधिनियम की धारा 9 के अंतर्गत आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) को लिखित शिकायत प्रस्तुत की जानी आवश्यक है, और धारा 11 के तहत प्राकृतिक न्याय के सिद्धांतों के अनुसार औपचारिक जांच की जाती है। बिना जांच या लिखित शिकायत के तुरंत निलंबन करना प्रशासनिक न्याय के विरुद्ध है।
कारण (R) के संदर्भ में: आधिकारिक उत्तर कुंजी के अनुसार विकल्प D को सही उत्तर माना गया है, जो यह स्पष्ट करता है कि अभिकथन A निश्चित रूप से गलत है। अधिनियम की धारा 12 के तहत अंतरिम राहत (जैसे स्थानांतरण, 3 महीने तक का सवैतनिक अवकाश आदि) व्यथित महिला के लिखित अनुरोध पर ICC द्वारा की जाने वाली विवेकाधीन अनुशंसाएं होती हैं, जबकि औपचारिक निलंबन सेवा नियमों (जैसे CCS (CCA) नियमावली) के तहत अनुशासनिक प्राधिकारी का अधिकार क्षेत्र है। मौखिक शिकायत पर स्वतः निलंबन अवैध होने के कारण अभिकथन A असत्य है। अतः विकल्प D सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) A is false but R is true

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 2(o)(i) of the POSH Act, 2013, a 'workplace' includes any department, organization, undertaking, establishment, enterprise, institution, office, branch or unit thereof which is established, owned, controlled or wholly or substantially financed by funds provided directly or indirectly by the appropriate Government or local authority. questions.question_english: Can a Government establishment be exempted from the mandatory provision of reserving vacancies for persons with benchmark disabilities under the RPwD Act, 2016?

questions.explanation_english:
While Section 34(1) of the RPwD Act, 2016 mandates a minimum 4% reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities in every Government establishment, the first proviso to Section 34(1) expressly provides for exemptions:
'Provided that the appropriate Government may, having regard to the type of work carried on in any department or establishment, by notification and subject to such conditions, if any, as may be specified in such notification, exempt any establishment from the provisions of this section.'

Such exemption cannot be granted arbitrarily or by an individual Head of Department; it requires an official gazette notification by the appropriate Government (Central or State Government), typically in consultation with the Chief Commissioner or State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (e.g., combatant units of armed forces or paramilitary forces).

questions.explanation_english:
The RPwD Act, 2016 maintains a vital distinction between general disability and benchmark disability:
1. Section 2(s) defines a 'person with disability' as a person with long-term physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory impairment which, in interaction with barriers, hinders their full and effective participation in society equally with others.
2. Section 2(r) defines a 'person with benchmark disability' as a person with not less than forty percent (40%) of a specified disability (as certified by a certifying medical authority), or a person with disability where specified disability has not been defined in measurable terms.
A certified benchmark disability (minimum 40%) is a statutory prerequisite to claim reservations in higher educational institutions (Section 32, minimum 5%), government employment (Section 34, minimum 4%), free education up to 18 years of age (Section 31), and priority in government welfare schemes.

questions.question_english: Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBVs) are residential schools established to promote education among girls belonging to disadvantaged groups. What is the mandated reservation quota for girls belonging to SC, ST, OBC, and Minority communities in these institutions?

Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Income under the head 'Salaries' is taxable during the financial year in which it becomes due or is received, whichever is earlier.
Reason (R): Arrears of salary received in the current year, which were not taxed in earlier years, are completely exempt from tax in the year of receipt.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options_english: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is true, but (R) is false
(A) is false, but (R) is true
questions.explanation_english:
Assertion (A) is true: Under Section 15 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, salary is taxable on a due basis or receipt basis, whichever occurs earlier. 
Reason (R) is false: Under Section 15(c), any arrears of salary paid or allowed to an employee in the previous year by or on behalf of an employer, if not charged to income-tax for any earlier previous year, are fully taxable in the year of receipt. They are not exempt from tax. However, to alleviate the hardship caused by higher tax slabs due to bunching of income, the assessee is eligible to claim tax relief under Section 89(1) by submitting Form 10E. Thus, (A) is true but (R) is false.

questions.question_english: A parent of a child admitted under the Economically Weaker Section (EWS) quota in a private unaided recognized school submits a written complaint to the Principal, stating that the school is demanding fees for textbooks and uniform contrary to RTE rules. What is the legally correct and mandatory response of the Principal?
options_english: Reject the complaint stating books and uniforms are never free in private schools
Provide books and uniforms free, seeking reimbursement from the State
Advise the parent to transfer the child to a state school if unable to pay costs
Forward the complaint to the local police department for extortion inquiry
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 12(1)(c) and Section 12(2) of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, private unaided recognized schools admitting children under the 25% EWS and Disadvantaged Group (DG) quota must provide free and compulsory elementary education. High Courts across the country, notably the Delhi High Court in landmark rulings (such as 'Justice for All v. Govt. of NCT of Delhi' and 'Federation of Public Schools v. GNCTD'), have conclusively held that 'free education' is not restricted merely to tuition fees. It includes the mandatory provision of free textbooks, writing materials, and school uniforms, as financial barriers in purchasing these essential materials prevent underprivileged children from participating equally in school. The school is legally prohibited from charging any money from the parents for these entitlements; instead, the school management must supply them free of cost and seek per-child statutory reimbursement from the State Government under Section 12(2).

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the inquiry procedure conducted by the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC):
I. The parties are permitted to bring legal practitioners to represent their case before the ICC.
II. The ICC has the power to make an ex-parte decision if the respondent fails to appear for three consecutive hearings without sufficient cause.
III. The ICC must serve a 15-day advance written notice to the party concerned before passing an ex-parte order.
IV. The inquiry of the ICC must be concluded within 60 days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
III and IV only
I, II, and IV only
questions.explanation_english:
Let us analyze each statement based on the POSH Act, 2013 and POSH Rules, 2013:
1. Statement I is incorrect: Rule 7(6) of the POSH Rules, 2013 expressly prohibits legal representation, stating that 'The parties shall not be allowed to bring any legal practitioner to represent them in their case at any stage of the proceedings before the Complaints Committee.'
2. Statement II is correct: Under Rule 7(5), the Complaints Committee has the right to terminate the inquiry proceedings or to give an ex-parte decision on the complaint, if the complainant or respondent fails, without sufficient cause, to present herself or himself for three consecutive hearings convened by the Chairperson or Presiding Officer.
3. Statement III is correct: The proviso to Rule 7(5) mandates that such termination or ex-parte order cannot be passed without giving a notice in writing, 15 days in advance, to the party concerned.
4. Statement IV is incorrect: Under Section 11(4) of the POSH Act, 2013, the inquiry must be completed within 90 days, not 60 days.
Therefore, only Statements II and III are correct.

Exchanging reserved vacancies among disability categories if unfulfilled in the succeeding year
Replacing an existing general category employee with a newly recruited disabled candidate

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 34(2) of the RPwD Act, 2016, where in any recruitment year any vacancy cannot be filled up due to the non-availability of a suitable person with benchmark disability, or for any other sufficient reasons, such vacancy is carried forward to the succeeding recruitment year. If in the succeeding recruitment year also a suitable person with benchmark disability is not available, the vacancy may first be filled by interchange among the five specified disability categories (clauses (a) to (e)). Only when there is no person with disability available for the post in that year even after interchange, may the employer fill up the vacancy by appointment of a person other than a person with disability. Thus, 'interchangeability' specifically refers to exchanging unfilled reserved vacancies among designated disability categories.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 34(2) के अनुसार, यदि किसी भर्ती वर्ष में बेंचमार्क दिव्यांगजनों हेतु आरक्षित कोई रिक्ति उपयुक्त अभ्यर्थी के अभाव या अन्य पर्याप्त कारणों से नहीं भरी जा सकती, तो उस रिक्ति को अगले भर्ती वर्ष में अग्रेषित (carry forward) किया जाता है। यदि अगले भर्ती वर्ष में भी उस विशिष्ट दिव्यांगता श्रेणी का उपयुक्त अभ्यर्थी नहीं मिलता है, तो सबसे पहले उस रिक्ति को धारा 34(1) की पाँच श्रेणियों [(a) से (e)] के बीच परस्पर विनिमय (interchange) द्वारा भरा जा सकता है। विनिमय के बाद भी यदि कोई दिव्यांग व्यक्ति उपलब्ध न हो, केवल तभी उस पद को गैर-दिव्यांग व्यक्ति की नियुक्ति द्वारा भरा जा सकता है। अतः 'परस्पर विनिमेयता' का तात्पर्य आरक्षित रिक्तियों को विभिन्न दिव्यांग श्रेणियों में परस्पर स्थानांतरित करने से है।

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 16(ia) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, a salaried individual (or a pensioner) is entitled to a standard deduction from gross salary of up to ₹50,000 or the amount of the salary, whichever is less, for the Financial Year 2023-24 (Assessment Year 2024-25).
